newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber down on Japan, Thanksgiving blues.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber down on Japan, Thanksgiving blues.

text.p: Rubber futures ended easier on Thursday as lower prices in Japan and the long Thanksgiving holiday in the U.S. compounded the market's blues, dealers said.
"With the Thanksgiving holiday in the (United) States and a fall in Japanese prices, many players opted to take a long break and stay away," a Singapore-based rubber trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark May contract fell 1.3 yen to end at 142.2 while Kobe's May contract ended at 141.7 from 142.5.
"The only thing that trimmed any further losses were some buying for RSS3 rubber and shortcovering for TSR20 rubber," another trader said.
About 775 tonnes of the January RSS3 contract were bought while 900 tonnes of the January TSR20 contract were also sold.
"The volumes on the other months were no encouraging. The market may well drift tomorrow," one dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 124.00-125.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 125.75 cents.
January RSS1 was untraded and indicated at 179.00-181.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27-$1.29) a kg from 181.25 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 174.00-176.00 Singapore cents (US$1.24-$1.26) a kg from 175.25 cents.
